title: Tenant safeguard and rollback coordination for 'sticky canary' model artifacts
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: Several customers reported persistent degraded outputs after a canary rollout in Dedicated and Private deployments where the new model variant continued serving to a tenant slice even after the canary mark was removed (we've started calling this 'sticky canary'). Investigation shows a combination of cached KV state + routing table staleness + tenant-slice affinity causing a subset of requests to be routed to servers still holding the new weights. Goal: define a containment protocol that minimizes customer impact, gives clear cross-team choreography (SRE, Serving, Router, Account Support), and a quick rollback/hotpatch path that works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments.
acceptance_criteria: Containment runbook validated in staging with a simulated sticky canary repro
Automated route-fence API available to temporarily isolate tenant slices within 2 minutes
KV cache invalidation steps documented and safe for multi-tenant Dedicated pools
Communication templates for customer liaison (initial, mid-update, resolution) ready
Post-incident checklist and follow-up ticket creation automated in PagerDuty or Linear
proposed_steps: 1) Immediate: On detection, run route-fence to pin affected tenant slice to known-good model variant (commands below).
2) Quarantine: For Dedicated/Private, trigger orchestration to drain worker nodes with suspected sticky state from the tenant slice (evacuate requests, wait for KV eviction).
3) KV reconciliation: Execute KV cache scrub job for affected model key prefixes; for on-prem, provide customer-safe script and checklist.
4) Verify: Run a fast automated prompt set (canary smoke suite) against the tenant slice to confirm outputs are back to baseline.

5) Rollback/Hotpatch: If scrub + fence fails, cut a tactical rollback: pin tenant routepolicy to previous model version and scale back canary rollout. For Hosted, leverage model fallbacks with immediate traffic shift; for Dedicated, update VM assignment and restart workers as necessary.
6) Customer comms: Use templated messages and assign customer liaison to provide ETA and next steps. Log conversation in account ticket and link to incident runbook.

7) Postmortem: Capture timeline, metric deltas (latency, token error rate, hallucination score), and decide long-term fixes (routing TTL reduction, KV eviction on model swap, stronger handshake between router and serving control-plane).
runbook_snippet:
Communication templates and quick commands:
- Slack incident channel: #inc-canary-<ticket>
- Initial message: 'We detected anomalous outputs for your account following a canary rollout. We are isolating your tenant slice and will update within 30 minutes with mitigation steps.'
- Route-fence API: curl -X POST https://router-api.internal/v1/route-fence -d '{"tenant":"<TENANT_ID>","model":"<GOOD_MODEL_TAG>","ttl_sec":3600}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <SRE_TOKEN>'
- KV scrub example: python tools/kv_scrub.py --env=prod --model-prefix=model-XYZ --tenant=<TENANT_ID> --dry-run=false
- Verification command: python tools/canary_smoke.py --tenant=<TENANT_ID> --suite=quick --expected=baseline.json
Note: For Private deployments, use the packaged onprem-scripts/kv_scrub.sh and coordinate with customer infra owner before execution.
